minor.issue: Volume/issue/pages (2021;39(10):1088-1095) not verifiable from the source, which lists only online publication 29 Dec 2020 and DOI; abbreviated author list.

Says deficit and asymmetry scores 'related weakly to general jump and speed performance'; the paper correlated deficits with jump/power tests only, and the finding was no significant relationship, not weak relationships with speed.

Labels deficit/asymmetry correlations 'small'; source reports non-significant r up to -0.31/-0.32 (moderate magnitude, CIs crossing zero). Omits Kappa values, perfect 505 vs COD-deficit asymmetry agreement, and that deficits did not differ by position.
Omits half squat and jump squat mean propulsive power tests, the kappa/correlation/Hedges g analyses, and the team/position split (13 forwards, 12 backs).

Omits the authors' explicit statement that the study was under-powered (21 per group required) and the >10% CVs for GCT and DEC-deficit; 'no between-session reliability' is asserted without source support.
Clearance criteria (symptoms, movement quality, rugby exposure) are generic and not drawn from the study, which tested uninjured players only.
'Backs and forwards differ in ... jump power' slightly overgeneralises; squat jump did not differ significantly.

note: Neither record misstates the source materially, but B reports the exact kappa, effect-size and correlation values, the under-powered sample and CV limits, and correctly bounds RTP use, whereas A is vaguer and pads practical fields with generic advice.
